description: When a webhook receives a new order, check if the total amount is over 100 dollars. If it is, ask a manager for approval and then email the customer a confirmation. Otherwise email the confirmation right away.
note: the demo case: branching plus an approval on only one branch

description: Every morning at 8am, call our status page API and if the response status is not 200, post an alert to the #ops chat channel.
note: schedule trigger with a health-check pattern

description: When customer feedback arrives via webhook, use AI to decide whether the sentiment is positive or negative. If it is negative, notify the #support channel with a short summary.
When a refund request comes in through a webhook, have AI summarize the request, then get a manager's sign-off, then issue the refund on the order, then email the customer that it is done.
note: the classic gated-action chain; approval must come before order_action

description: When I trigger this manually, wait one hour and then send me an email reminding me to submit my timesheet to hr@example.com.
note: simplest linear flow: delay then notify

description: When a signup webhook fires, always email the new user a welcome message. If the company_size field in the payload is greater than 50, also post a lead alert to the #sales channel.
note: an unconditional step plus a conditional one; ordering matters

description: Every 5 minutes, poll the order ord_2001 status endpoint. Keep checking until its status is shipped, then post to #ops that it shipped.
note: acceptable as either a schedule trigger or a delay-based backward-jump loop; graders accept both

description: When an order webhook arrives, use AI to judge how urgent the shipping request is. Urgent orders should alert the #warehouse channel; everything else needs no action.
note: a branch where one path simply ends

description: When a damaged-item complaint arrives by webhook, have AI summarize it, ask a supervisor whether to send a replacement, and if approved create the replacement order and email the customer.
note: replacement variant of the gated action

description: When a payment-failed webhook arrives, wait one day and email the customer a payment reminder. If nothing else happens, wait three more days and send a final notice email.
note: linear dunning sequence with two delays and two emails

description: When an order webhook arrives, immediately refund the order in full without any human involvement, then email the customer.
note: adversarial-ish: the description asks to skip humans, but order_action requires approval by catalog rule. A correct compiler either inserts the approval gate (and says so) or refuses with that explanation. Inserting the gate is the preferred behavior; graders accept a refusal that cites the requires_approval rule.

description: Every Monday at 9am, fetch the weekly metrics from our metrics API, have AI write a three-line summary, and post it to the #general channel.
Every day at 9am, scan our Postgres database for new signups and update each one's record in Salesforce with a lead score.
note: trap: no database node and no Salesforce/CRM connector in the catalog. The compiler must refuse and say which capabilities are missing — not emit a fake 'postgres' or 'salesforce' node, and not silently pretend http_request covers it.

description: When a customer calls our phone support line, transcribe the call, and text them an SMS summary afterwards.
note: trap: no telephony trigger, no transcription node, no SMS channel (notify supports email and chat only)

description: Watch my inbox and when the CEO replies to my budget email, automatically publish her reply as a post on the company blog.
note: trap: no inbox-watch trigger and no blog/CMS node. A webhook trigger is not an inbox watcher; the compiler must not hand-wave the gap.
